To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of children with positive skin prick tests to inhalant allergens at 18 years have had positive skin prick tests from 4 years of age and that the prevalence of skin prick test sensitization to inhalant allergen is stable from 4 to 18 years.

sensitization rates to food allergens, in particular to peanut and egg white, are high in early childhood, but decrease over time, whereas sensitization rates to aeroallergens, in particular grass pollen, are low in early childhood, and increase with age.

sensitization rates in the 1989 birth cohort increased from 7.8% at age 4 years to 17.3% at age 16 years, that sensitization to inhalant allergens was more common than to foods, and that the prevalence of multiple sensitizations increased with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the natural history of skin prick test reactivity to common allergens in a large birth cohort of children followed up prospectively from birth to the age of 18.
the natural history of cutaneous sensitization over the first 18 years of life.
the development of allergic diseases and their prevention, with particular emphasis on eczema and food allergy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPT is a reliable and safe method to assess sensitization to aeroallergens and food.
the prevalence of sensitization to food allergens in childhood and adolescence is high, but the clinical relevance is low.
the prevalence of SPT positivity to common allergens in children and adults has increased significantly in the last 20 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are significant changes in sensitization to common allergens over childhood and adolescence, with a peak in sensitization at around 12 years, and a decline after this age.
there is no single, simple answer for the question of what causes asthma and that the answer depends on the population studied.

there is no evidence of a general decline in SPT positivity in the first 2 decades of life, but rather that the pattern of sensitization is changing with a reduction in food allergen sensitization being accompanied by an increase in sensitization to aeroallergens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the natural history of sensitization to food allergens is complex, and it is difficult to predict who is at risk of persistent sensitization.
the prevalence of SPT positivity to aeroallergens is relatively low in early childhood, increases in the early teenage years, and then plateaus or declines.
sensitisation is a dynamic process that can change over time, even in children with no symptoms.
